name: browser
description: Browser automation for linked accounts. Each account has its own private profile on the host, a virtual display and a live VNC view. Only the user can take control. A network proxy that enforces rules protects every session.

configSchema.label: Runtime
configSchema.hint: Chrome detection and process limits for each account. The browser starts only when the enforcing proxy and a safe Chrome sandbox are available.

configSchema.label: Chrome executable
configSchema.hint: Optional full path to Chrome or Chromium. Leave empty to use a supported system browser.

configSchema.label: Active accounts
configSchema.hint: Maximum number of Chrome processes running at once, one for each account.

configSchema.label: Tab sessions per account
configSchema.hint: Maximum number of tab sessions one account may keep open in its Chrome process.

configSchema.label: Idle timeout
configSchema.hint: Close a browser session after this long without agent, user or viewer activity.

configSchema.label: Hard session limit
configSchema.hint: Total time for one browser session, including time under your control.

configSchema.label: Process close grace
configSchema.hint: How long Chrome stays available after the account's last tab closes. The profile stays on disk.

configSchema.label: Live view
configSchema.hint: Each account's Chrome appears on a private virtual display and streams over VNC. When taking control, the user sends real keyboard and mouse input. Xvfb and x11vnc must be installed on the host.

configSchema.label: Display width
configSchema.hint: Virtual display size. The page itself is shorter because Chrome's tab strip and address bar take up space.

configSchema.label: Viewers per session
configSchema.hint: Each viewer gets the full screen image. The VNC server creates a separate stream for each connection and cannot shrink it for a small window.

configSchema.label: Update coalescing
configSchema.hint: How long the VNC server gathers screen changes before sending them. Measured at 1280×800: 10 ms reacts in 88 ms and uses about 590 kB/s while scrolling. 40 ms uses about 370 kB/s but reacts in 146 ms.

configSchema.label: Takeover lease
configSchema.hint: User control must confirm it is still active within this interval. An old window cannot extend or release a newer takeover.

configSchema.label: Chrome targets per account
configSchema.hint: Includes pages, popups, workers and other Chrome targets. New targets over the limit are closed.

configSchema.label: Network policy
configSchema.hint: All Chrome traffic must pass through a local proxy. Before connecting, it checks, approves and pins the destination address.

configSchema.label: Proxy concurrency
configSchema.hint: Number of connections Chrome may keep open through the proxy at once. A page with many images can open dozens across different content delivery networks (CDNs). Each request over the limit fails with ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED, and images do not load. Lower the limit only to deliberately restrict an account.

configSchema.label: Proxy requests per minute
configSchema.hint: Request limit per minute for the whole account. Normal browsing uses several hundred a minute, so a low limit leaves pages only partly loaded.

configSchema.label: Private network allowlist
configSchema.hint: Exact hostnames or CIDR ranges explicitly allowed for local development. An empty list blocks private, loopback, link-local and metadata networks.

strings.accountDescription: Your private Chrome profile keeps sign-ins between sessions on this Elowen installation.
strings.settingsDescription: Live capacity and isolation status for managed Chrome sessions.
strings.agentWaiting: The agent is waiting for you to return control
strings.closeConfirmDescription: The live view and tab will close. Your browser profile and sign-ins remain stored.
strings.liveCapacityHint: Only counts active Chrome processes and tab sessions. Browser content remains private to its account.
strings.isolationHint: Every account has a separate persistent profile and Chrome process. All traffic must cross the pinned enforcing proxy.
strings.limitsHint: The limits above apply before Chrome, a virtual display or a live view connection starts.
strings.limitsBody: Sessions close automatically after the idle or maximum time limit. A live view sends the full image over one VNC connection. Only the account that took control can operate the browser.
strings.depsHint: Everything a managed browser session needs to start. These checks only read data. The sandbox and DevTools connection are checked on first managed launch.
strings.dep_display_ready: Xvfb and x11vnc are installed and executable.
strings.dep_display_missing: A managed browser is drawn on a private X display, and this host is missing what serves it.
strings.dep_display_missing_fix: Install the Xvfb and x11vnc packages on this host, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_liveview_ready: This host carries plugin WebSocket routes.
strings.dep_liveview_missing: This host cannot carry a plugin WebSocket, so sessions run without a live view or user takeover.
strings.dep_liveview_missing_fix: Update Elowen to a release that offers plugin WebSocket routes.
strings.dep_chrome_missing: No supported Chrome or Chromium executable was found on this computer.
strings.dep_chrome_missing_fix: Install Google Chrome or Chromium, or enter the path to the executable in the plugin settings.
strings.dep_chrome_unusable: The configured executable is missing or cannot be executed by the daemon account.
strings.dep_chrome_unusable_fix: Correct the path to the Chrome executable in the plugin settings, or clear it to find the file automatically.
strings.dep_control_missing: puppeteer-core is missing from the daemon runtime, or does not expose launch().
strings.dep_control_missing_fix: The plugin uses the same runtime dependencies as the Elowen daemon. Reinstall or update Elowen with these dependencies, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_proxy_missing: The proxy-chain 3.0 library could not be loaded, so the browser cannot start.
strings.dep_proxy_missing_fix: The plugin shares the Elowen daemon’s runtime dependencies: reinstall or update Elowen with its runtime dependencies, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_proxy_unsupported: The proxy adapter cannot pin DNS per request, so the browser cannot start.
strings.dep_proxy_unsupported_fix: Restore the bundled proxy adapter. A browser session can only reach computers whose address was checked by the navigation rules.
strings.dep_storage_unwritable: The profile directory cannot be written by the daemon account.
strings.dep_storage_unwritable_fix: Give the daemon account write access to the plugin data directory, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_storage_exposed: The profile directory is readable beyond the daemon account.
strings.dep_storage_exposed_fix: Restrict the plugin data directory to owner-only access, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_storage_missing: The profile directory is no longer the trusted directory the plugin created.
strings.dep_storage_missing_fix: Restore the plugin data directory as a regular directory owned by the daemon account, then restart the daemon.
strings.dep_artifacts_missing: This computer has no connection for displaying content directly in chat. Sessions therefore will not appear as live cards in chat.
strings.dep_artifacts_missing_fix: Update Elowen to a release that supports inline chat artifacts.
strings.profileStorageHint: Cookies and sign-ins are stored only in your account profile. Live view images are never stored.
strings.clearBlocked: Close every running session before the profile can be cleared.
strings.liveSessionsHint: Closing a tab session does not erase your saved browser profile.
strings.noSessionsDescription: A session appears here when your agent opens the browser.
strings.previewPending: Waiting for a picture of this session
strings.clearConfirmDescription: Stored cookies, sign-ins and site data will be permanently removed. This cannot be undone.
